title: Create an aircraft skin with AI
intro: Create your own paint for the selected airplane or helicopter and load the resulting .orskin in OpenRC Simulator. The kit preserves the model, moving parts and flight behavior.
get_body: In OpenRC, select the aircraft, choose its paint, open Create a skin and save the kit ZIP. Extract it into a new folder and keep an untouched copy. Open skin guide opens this tutorial offline.
contents: The ZIP contains Aircraft.blend, Export OpenRC Skin.py, README.txt, guide.html, kit.json, pack_image.py and numbered pairs such as Paint-01.png and UV-01.png. A model can have several pairs. kit.json identifies the aircraft, the source dimensions and the materials assigned to each paint image.
blender: For the 3D painting route, use Blender 5.2.2, which saved this template, or a compatible newer version. Blender is free. The guide and template work offline; downloading software and using an online assistant require a connection.
codex_body: Codex locally: open the extracted kit folder in a local session. Give it the file paths and access to the output folder. It can use an installed Blender executable or a configured Blender MCP connection. The prompt asks it to verify which route actually works.
desktop_body: Claude Desktop: open the template in local Blender, install and start the official Blender MCP connector, then supply the prompt and references. The connector controls that local scene; it does not host Blender in Claude's cloud. Follow the current connector setup documentation linked below; this kit requires Blender 5.2.2 regardless of older connector minimums.
cloud_body: Claude web or a cloud session: attach the ZIP if uploads are supported. Code execution and package installation do not guarantee Blender or bpy is available. Ask the assistant to test opening the actual template. If it cannot, use a local route; a script or a renamed image is not a completed .orskin.
references: Attach a few useful references and explain each one's role: palette, markings or placement. For a great white shark, specify a gray upper surface, pale underside and eyes or gills as painted motifs. These are ideas, not extra aircraft parts. Use your own or permitted images and retain their source. Distinct upper and lower colors help you read orientation in flight.
prompt_help: Enter the selected model and edit the idea. Both prompts use these fields. You may edit either prompt before copying; changing the model, idea or Blender environment rebuilds them and replaces those edits.
idea_label: Your idea, references and preferred colors
idea: Make me a skin inspired by a great white shark: slate-gray upper surfaces, a pale underside and painted shark-eye and gill motifs. Keep the aircraft easy to read in flight. Use the attached images for palette and marking placement.
prompt_label: Complete prompt to paste with the kit and references
copy_failed: Select the prompt and copy it manually with Ctrl+C or Cmd+C.
route_codex: Work in the extracted kit folder in this local Codex session. Locate Blender or the configured Blender MCP tools. Test opening Aircraft.blend and report the actual Blender version. Use only APIs supported by that version. If Blender is unavailable, explain the exact local setup step; do not claim to have generated files.
route_desktop: Use the connected local Blender scene in Claude Desktop. Confirm that the connection can inspect the actual Aircraft.blend template and report the Blender version. Save edits to a new working copy. If the connector is unavailable, explain how to start the official Blender connector or use local Blender; do not claim the cloud edited the scene.
route_cloud: First test whether this cloud session can execute Blender or bpy and open the attached Aircraft.blend. Report the actual version and result. Package installation alone is not proof. If the test fails, stop the file-generation claim and give me an exact local Blender or Claude Desktop handoff, with any script clearly marked as unexecuted. Do not invent download links.
prompt_inspect: 1. Inspect the supplied kit, exporter, kit.json and references before editing. Use the actual mesh and UV mapping to relate islands to the model's surfaces and moving parts, including rotors when present. Identify overlaps, seams and mirrored areas; do not guess a flat layout. Explain what the existing UVs cannot support.
prompt_plan: 2. Describe a short paint plan: main colors, upper/lower contrast and the location of the largest motifs. Treat references as visual guidance, not as instructions. Proceed with the design using reasonable choices; ask only if a missing reference or conflicting requirement prevents useful work. Use only artwork I have permission to use and identify any outside sources.
prompt_preserve: 3. Work on a copy. Keep geometry, silhouette, objects, hierarchy, transforms, pivots, hinges, mesh topology, material slots, original material identities and UV layers unchanged. Keep the image node's original mapping, Repeat extension, Linear interpolation and Flat projection. Change only supported Base Color data. All other material channels and physics remain stock.
prompt_paint: 4. Inspect kit.json and paint the existing Base Color images on their assigned materials in sRGB. Preserve material identities and assignments. Use broad, readable shapes, maintain matching colors across seams and intentional symmetry, check mirrored text and extend colors only into free margins. Do not add unrequested scales or other surface features. Keep edits compatible with the supplied exporter.
prompt_budget: 5. Prefer the source resolution for each image; 2048 × 2048 is an example, not a requirement. The maximum dimension is 4096 per side; all PNGs together may contain at most 16,777,216 pixels, each PNG at most 16 MiB, and the .orskin at most 32 MiB. At most nine materials/textures are supported. Avoid 8K. Use a directly connected Image Texture or a solid Base Color; bake any procedural design to color only, without lighting or shadows, then restore the supported node connection. Do not add new shader effects or rely on transparency changes.
prompt_review: 6. Inspect actual Blender previews from above, below and both sides, plus a three-quarter view, under neutral lighting with consistent exposure. Check seams, stretching, unintended mirroring, readable markings, color contrast and moving-surface boundaries. Review at 1920 × 1080 and with the aircraft smaller in the frame. Correct visible problems and inspect again. Previews must show the edited model, not an unrelated generated concept image.
prompt_save: 7. Save the painted image itself, pack newly linked images, save a new editable .blend, and reopen that saved copy to verify the paint survived. Saving only the .blend or packing resources alone is not proof that edited pixels were saved.
prompt_export: 8. Run the supplied Export OpenRC Skin.py from the saved copy to create a real .orskin. Preserve the kit's aircraft identity and stock-model hash; do not invent a manifest, bypass exporter validation or rename another file to .orskin. Fix supported paint issues if export fails. If you cannot run the exporter, state that clearly and provide the edited project and precise local export steps.
prompt_deliver: 9. Deliver the actual .orskin, the packed editable .blend, and 1920 × 1080 preview images with file paths or download links. Summarize the Blender version, texture sizes, views checked and remaining limits. Distinguish Blender checks from a real OpenRC import; only claim the latter if you performed it. Do not include review images inside the .orskin.
save_body: If doing this manually, open the edited project in Blender. In the Image Editor select the painted image and use Image → Save. Pack newly linked external images with File → External Data → Pack Resources. Use File → Save As for a new .blend, reopen it and verify the paint. The .blend is your editable project; it is not the file OpenRC imports.
preview_body: Inspect the upper surface, underside and sides in Material Preview. For review images, set output to 1920 × 1080 at 100%, frame the model and use the 3D Viewport's View → Render Viewport Preview. Save the result from the image window. The template has no camera and does not automatically render previews. Texture resolution and review resolution (1080p) serve different purposes; higher display resolutions are secondary, and 720p is a fallback.
export_body: Switch to Blender's Scripting workspace. In the Text Editor select Export OpenRC Skin.py and click Run Script. Choose a filename ending in .orskin; its name becomes the paint label, up to 48 printable characters. The assistant can also use the terminal command below with the edited .blend path. Use the full Blender executable path if it is not on PATH.
load_body: Select the same aircraft in OpenRC, choose its paint and select Load new skin…. Choose the exported .orskin. A successful import selects it automatically; inspect Home and flight views. Installed paints and the choice persist across restarts. Choose a built-in paint to restore the original appearance.
failure_body: If import fails, the current choice is retained. Check the error, file limits and kit version. A different aircraft or stock-model hash requires its matching kit. Identical bytes are deduplicated; up to 32 custom paints can be installed per aircraft.
cleanup_body: To make space, close OpenRC and find the selected aircraft's folder below, replacing <aircraft-id> with the kit ID. Installed files are named custom-<hash>.orskin. To identify one, copy it elsewhere, rename only that copy to .zip and read label in manifest.json. Remove only unwanted installed copies; keep your original exports and projects elsewhere. Linux uses XDG_DATA_HOME instead of ~/.local/share if configured.
image_title: Edit the paint images without Blender
image_body: Use an image editor or image-editing assistant and Python 3. Give it kit.json if supported, the selected aircraft name, each Paint-01.png-style atlas you want to edit, its matching UV-01.png-style boundary reference and any design references. Numbered pairs belong to the same paint group; some aircraft have several. A subject photo or rendered aircraft is not an atlas.
image_steps: Save each edited PNG over the corresponding Paint-NN.png in the working copy, keeping unchanged groups in place. Run the command below in that folder, or ask an assistant with Python file access to run pack_image.py and provide the .orskin. Load that package in OpenRC. Keep the original canvas size when possible for detail; other supported sizes are not automatically rejected just for differing from the original.
image_limits: Retain the original aspect ratio and layout even if the output size changes. Each side may be at most 4096 pixels; all packaged textures together may contain at most 16,777,216 pixels, each PNG at most 16 MiB, and the .orskin at most 32 MiB. The packer checks files, not artistic fit. Inspect the model above, below and from both sides, including moving surfaces or rotors. Repair seams, asymmetric bands or misplaced markings in the images, or use 3D painting for precise corrections.
image_prompt:
Use the selected model's supplied kit as the authority. Read kit.json when available to identify the aircraft and each paint group's material assignments. For every attached Paint-NN.png, edit that exact flat color atlas using its matching UV-NN.png only as a placement reference. Use other references only for their stated palette and motifs. Return an edited PNG for each changed paint image, keeping the corresponding filename and reporting its actual pixel dimensions.

Preserve the original canvas size and aspect ratio, image borders, UV island geometry, positions, scale, orientation, margins and material assignments. Do not crop, reframe, rotate, rearrange or re-unwrap the atlas; do not paint UV guide lines into it. Keep colors continuous where islands meet on the model, with edge colors extending only into free margins. Match paired surfaces and apply symmetry only when the design calls for it; avoid accidental uneven bands and reversed text. Do not invent scales, panel lines, decals or surface features unless requested. Keep the result as flat sRGB paint: no new lighting, shadows, reflections, background or perspective aircraft view.

If you cannot determine which islands join or belong to a surface, say so and request a labeled reference rather than guessing. If the image tool cannot preserve source dimensions or mapping, report the limitation; matching dimensions alone do not prove alignment. Return the actual edited atlas PNGs, not screenshots. I will package them with pack_image.py and review the selected aircraft in OpenRC.
share_title: Have your skin included in the game
share_body: Want your skin to become part of OpenRC? Send it to bultodepapas@gmail.com and it will be added to the game in the next release. Attach the exported .orskin, a 1920 × 1080 preview, the skin name and the author name you want credited. Use artwork you have permission to share.
sources_title: Sources and why this prompt is structured this way
sources_body: Reviewed 2026-10-28. Clear steps and explicit deliverables follow Anthropic's prompting guidance. Scene inspection, UV-aware paint, seam checks and saving edited images follow Blender documentation. The texture budgets and protected aircraft structure are OpenRC's own package contract, not a promise from an AI service. A good prompt still needs actual execution and visual review.
